  subcommand), the claude prompt, and the crew reply/msg body are recognised as data. The
  exemption is withdrawn whenever the program's identity can't be trusted — an impersonated
  resolution (exec -a, sudo -u, env -S, path-invoked wrapper, leading quoted "NAME=value",
  env <number>) or any in-command redefinition (function/alias/hash/trap, BASH_CMDS/PATH/…
  incl. quote-split, opaque command word, or manufacturing a data-taker name).
  Unknown/renamed programs keep zero exemption, so every rename bypass stays denied. The
  three repros now pass; some-unknown-tool . and all round-1/round-2 probes stay denied.
  Pipeline (grid, deep tier):
  - Spec — spec-critic cap reached (initial + 3 rounds); every finding folded (including
    the critic-sanctioned final two).
  - Plan — accept after 1 revision. (A Claude Code safety-classifier model-switch dialog
    briefly blocked the plan-critic pane on the probe-laden plan; the dispatcher cleared
    it; I discarded an empty-body and a stale pre-edit verdict before the real accept.)
  - Execute — opus agent (gate code + tests, red-green), sonnet agent (docs); I verified
    all 4 deviations and reconciled the README.
  - Fast gate — green (race, both golangci-lint, nilaway).
  - Code review — review_mode: full, review_high: 0; security-reviewer Approve (60+
    probes), two mechanical MEDIUMs from go/general reviewers fixed, one security
    non-finding declined (below bar).
  - Deslop → push → PR → CI green → pr_open → done.
  One thing I'd flag for your awareness: the plan-phase safety-classifier dialog required a
  dispatcher intervention (answering the model-switch prompt) — the attack-probe strings
  in a security-tooling plan reliably trip the classifier, which is worth noting if this
  recurs on similar guard work.
